blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Concrete Driveway Cost in Geelong in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out how much a concrete driveway costs in Geelong in 2026. We break down real pricing, finishes, and factors affecting your project budget.
body: If you are a Geelong homeowner wondering about the cost of a new concrete driveway in 2026, you are not alone. A driveway is one of the most impactful investments you can make for your property, boosting both kerb appeal and functionality across Geelong's diverse suburbs. At Vik Concreting Geelong, we have been installing driveways across the region for over seven years, and we understand that pricing depends on several key factors. From the size of your driveway and the concrete finish you choose to site accessibility and ground conditions in suburbs like Belmont, Lara, and Highton, every project is unique. In this guide, we break down the real costs Geelong homeowners can expect for a quality concrete driveway in 2026, so you can plan your budget with confidence.

The base cost of a standard plain concrete driveway in Geelong typically ranges from $50 to $75 per square metre for the concrete supply and placement alone. However, this figure only tells part of the story. When you factor in site preparation, which may include excavation, removing existing surfaces, levelling, and installing a proper sub-base of crushed rock, the total installed cost generally sits between $100 and $150 per square metre for a basic finish. In newer Geelong suburbs like Waurn Ponds or Armstrong Creek, where lots may have more level access, costs can be on the lower end. Older suburbs with tighter access, such as parts of Geelong West or Belmont, may incur additional costs due to skip bin hire for rubble removal or restricted machinery access. Getting a detailed on-site quote from a local concreter ensures there are no surprises.

For homeowners wanting something beyond plain grey concrete, exposed aggregate is one of the most popular choices across Geelong. This finish reveals the natural stone within the concrete mix, creating a textured, decorative surface that is both slip-resistant and visually striking. In 2026, exposed aggregate driveways in Geelong typically cost between $130 and $180 per square metre installed, depending on the aggregate type and colour you select. Coloured concrete, achieved by adding pigment to the mix, generally falls in a similar price range of $120 to $160 per square metre. Stamped or imitated concrete, which replicates the look of brick, tile, or stone, sits at the higher end at $150 to $200 per square metre. While these premium finishes require a larger upfront investment, they significantly enhance your Geelong property's value and street presence.

Several factors specific to Geelong can influence your driveway cost. The region's proximity to the coast means some suburbs experience higher salt exposure and moisture levels, which may require additional sealing or specialised concrete mixes designed for coastal conditions. Properties in low-lying areas or those near Corio Bay may need enhanced drainage solutions to prevent water pooling during heavy rain events, which are common in the Geelong region during winter months. Additionally, Victorian Building Authority regulations require driveways to meet specific fall and drainage standards, and any work near a nature strip or council road may require permits from the City of Greater Geelong Council. At Vik Concreting Geelong, we handle all permit requirements and ensure your driveway is fully compliant with local regulations from the outset.

A smart way to manage your driveway budget is to understand what is included in a comprehensive quote from your Geelong concreter. A thorough quote should itemise site preparation, including excavation depth and sub-base material, the concrete mix specification and finish, reinforcement such as steel mesh or fibres, edging and control joints, and final clean-up and curing. Be wary of quotes that seem unusually low, as they may exclude essential items like proper compaction of the sub-base or adequate steel reinforcement, both of which are critical for longevity in Geelong's variable climate. At Vik Concreting Geelong, we provide transparent, itemised quotes for every driveway project, so Geelong homeowners know exactly what they are paying for before any work begins.

The best time to pour a concrete driveway in Geelong is typically during the drier months from October through April, when consistent temperatures and lower rainfall allow for optimal curing. However, experienced concreters like Vik Concreting Geelong can work year-round by using appropriate curing compounds and timing pours around Geelong's weather patterns. Investing in a quality concrete driveway now can save you thousands in future repairs, as a well-installed driveway should last 25 to 30 years or more with minimal maintenance. For a personalised quote on your Geelong driveway project, contact Vik Concreting Geelong today on 0403 964 510 or request a free quote through our website. We serve Geelong and all surrounding suburbs including Lara, Belmont, Highton, and Waurn Ponds.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete in Geelong's Variable Climate
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the best time to pour concrete in Geelong's variable climate. Our guide covers seasonal conditions, curing tips, and year-round concreting advice.
body: Geelong's climate presents unique challenges for concrete pouring that every homeowner and builder should understand before starting a project. Located on the western side of Corio Bay, Geelong experiences a temperate oceanic climate with four distinct seasons, each bringing different conditions that can affect how concrete sets, cures, and ultimately performs over its lifetime. At Vik Concreting Geelong, with over seven years of local experience, we have poured concrete through scorching summer days, crisp autumn mornings, and everything in between. Understanding when conditions are optimal for concrete work in Geelong is essential for achieving a durable, crack-free finish that will serve your property for decades. In this comprehensive guide, we explore the best times to pour concrete in the Geelong region and how professional concreters adapt to local weather patterns.

Summer in Geelong, running from December through February, is generally considered the ideal window for concrete pouring. Average daytime temperatures between 25 and 35 degrees Celsius provide excellent conditions for hydration, the chemical process that allows concrete to gain strength. However, Geelong's summer heat is not without risks. When temperatures exceed 35 degrees, the surface moisture in freshly poured concrete can evaporate too quickly, leading to surface cracking and a weakened finish. This is particularly relevant in Geelong's northern suburbs like Corio and Norlane, where open, unshaded lots receive full sun exposure. Professional concreters counter this by scheduling pours for early morning, using curing compounds to seal surface moisture, and dampening the concrete surface during the critical first 24 hours. At Vik Concreting Geelong, we carefully monitor weather forecasts and adjust our pour schedules to ensure optimal results even during the hottest Geelong days.

Autumn and spring are transitional seasons that can offer surprisingly good concrete pouring conditions in Geelong. March through May and September through November typically bring mild temperatures between 12 and 22 degrees Celsius, which allows concrete to cure slowly and evenly without the rapid moisture loss of summer or the frost risks of winter. These moderate conditions often produce the highest quality concrete finishes, as the slower curing process allows for maximum strength development. For Geelong homeowners planning larger projects such as commercial slabs or extensive landscaping concrete works, these shoulder seasons may offer the best balance of weather reliability and contractor availability. Vik Concreting Geelong often recommends autumn as an excellent time for residential driveway and patio projects in suburbs like Belmont, Highton, and Waurn Ponds, where the milder conditions support flawless finishes.

Winter concrete pouring in Geelong requires the most careful planning but is absolutely achievable with the right expertise. From June through August, Geelong experiences average temperatures between 6 and 14 degrees Celsius, with regular rainfall and occasional frost, particularly in inland suburbs like Lara and Batesford. The main concern with winter pours is that cold temperatures significantly slow the hydration process, meaning concrete takes much longer to reach its design strength. If temperatures drop below 5 degrees Celsius, there is also a risk of frost damage to freshly poured concrete. However, experienced local concreters use insulated blankets, heated enclosures, and accelerated admixtures to maintain adequate curing temperatures. Vik Concreting Geelong has successfully completed numerous winter projects across the Geelong region by adapting our methods to suit the colder conditions, ensuring every pour meets Australian standards regardless of the season.

Beyond choosing the right season, several practical factors should influence the timing of your concrete project in Geelong. Soil conditions in the region vary significantly, from the sandy soils near the coast to heavier clay soils further inland, and each type behaves differently with moisture and temperature changes. Ground saturation from Geelong's winter rains can make site preparation more challenging and may require additional drainage work before pouring. Planning permission from the City of Greater Geelong Council may also affect your timeline, as permit approvals can take several weeks for residential and commercial concrete work. It is also worth considering the availability of materials and labour, as peak building season in Geelong typically runs from September to March, when demand for concreting services is highest. Booking your project with Vik Concreting Geelong well in advance ensures you secure your preferred dates.

At Vik Concreting Geelong, we understand that waiting for the perfect conditions is not always practical, which is why our team is equipped to pour concrete year-round across the Geelong region. Whether you are planning a new driveway in Lara, a commercial slab in Geelong's central business district, or landscaping concrete in Belmont, we assess local site conditions, weather forecasts, and your project requirements to determine the optimal pour schedule. Our seven years of experience pouring concrete in Geelong's variable climate means we know exactly how to adapt our techniques for consistent, high-quality results in any season. From early-morning summer pours to insulated winter installations, every project receives the same meticulous attention to detail that has earned Vik Concreting Geelong its reputation as one of the region's most reliable concrete contractors. For expert advice on timing your concrete project in Geelong, contact us today on 0403 964 510 for a free on-site assessment and personalised quote.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate vs Plain Concrete: Which Is Best for Geelong Homes?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing exposed aggregate and plain concrete for your Geelong home? We weigh up cost, durability, aesthetics, and suitability for local coastal conditions.
body: Choosing between exposed aggregate and plain concrete for your Geelong property is one of the most common decisions homeowners face when planning a new driveway, patio, or outdoor area. Both finishes have their merits, but the right choice depends on your budget, aesthetic preferences, and the specific demands of your Geelong location. At Vik Concreting Geelong, with over seven years of experience installing both finishes across the region, we have seen firsthand how each option performs in the local conditions. From the sandy soils near Corio Bay to the clay-heavy ground in suburbs like Highton and Waurn Ponds, Geelong's diverse landscape can influence which concrete finish is most suitable for your project. This guide compares exposed aggregate and plain concrete across the factors that matter most to Geelong homeowners.

Plain concrete, often referred to as a broom finish or trowel finish, is the most straightforward and cost-effective option for Geelong properties. The surface is finished with a broom or steel trowel to create a clean, uniform texture that provides adequate slip resistance and a neat appearance. In Geelong, plain concrete driveways typically cost between $100 and $150 per square metre installed, making them an attractive choice for homeowners working within a tighter budget. The finish is highly versatile and can be left in its natural grey colour or enhanced with concrete sealer for added protection against Geelong's coastal moisture. Plain concrete is particularly popular for shed floors, garage slabs, and utility areas where aesthetics are secondary to functionality. For Geelong investment properties or rental units in suburbs like Norlane or Corio, plain concrete offers an excellent balance of durability and affordability that appeals to both owners and tenants.

Exposed aggregate is a decorative concrete finish where the top layer of cement paste is removed to reveal the natural stone, pebbles, or glass aggregate embedded within the mix. This creates a textured, visually rich surface that is highly sought after for Geelong driveways, patios, and pool surrounds. The cost of exposed aggregate in Geelong ranges from $130 to $180 per square metre installed, reflecting the additional labour and materials required for the exposure process. One of the biggest advantages for Geelong homeowners is the wide range of aggregate options available, from warm earth tones that complement period homes in Geelong West to modern grey blends that suit contemporary builds in Armstrong Creek. The exposed stones provide excellent natural slip resistance, making exposed aggregate a practical choice for areas around swimming pools or slopes where wet-weather traction is important.

When comparing durability, both exposed aggregate and plain concrete perform well in Geelong's conditions, but there are important differences. Plain concrete's smooth surface is susceptible to showing tyre marks, oil stains, and surface wear over time, particularly on high-traffic driveways. In contrast, the textured surface of exposed aggregate naturally camouflages minor stains and wear, maintaining its appearance for longer with less visible aging. However, exposed aggregate requires a quality sealer to prevent the exposed stones from loosening over time, especially in Geelong's coastal suburbs where salt air can accelerate degradation. For properties in Lara, Corio, or any suburb within reach of Corio Bay's salt-laden winds, a resealing schedule every two to three years is recommended to maintain the aggregate's integrity and appearance. Plain concrete can also benefit from sealing but is generally lower maintenance in this regard.

Geelong's unique local conditions should also influence your decision between these two finishes. The region's clay soils, prevalent in suburbs like Highton, Belmont, and Grovedale, expand and contract with moisture changes, which can place stress on concrete surfaces. Both finishes can accommodate this movement when properly reinforced with steel mesh or fibres, but the textured surface of exposed aggregate tends to mask minor hairline cracks that may develop over time. In Geelong's flood-prone areas near the Barwon River, drainage is critical for any concrete installation, and both finishes should incorporate adequate falls to direct water away from your property. The City of Greater Geelong Council has specific requirements for stormwater management on residential properties, and your chosen concreter should ensure full compliance. Vik Concreting Geelong designs every project with local soil, drainage, and climate factors in mind.

Ultimately, the choice between exposed aggregate and plain concrete comes down to your priorities as a Geelong homeowner. If budget is the primary concern and you need a clean, functional surface for a shed, garage, or rental property, plain concrete delivers reliable performance at the lowest cost. If you want to enhance your Geelong property's kerb appeal and create a stunning outdoor living space that neighbours will admire, exposed aggregate offers a premium finish that adds genuine value to your home. For many Geelong clients, a practical approach is to use plain concrete for utility areas and exposed aggregate for front-facing driveways and entertainment spaces. At Vik Concreting Geelong, we provide honest, no-pressure advice to help you choose the right finish for your specific property and budget. Contact us for a free on-site quote across Geelong and surrounding suburbs.

blogPosts.title: Concrete Solutions for Geelong's Coastal and Bay-Side Properties
blogPosts.excerpt: Concrete near the coast faces unique challenges. Discover how Geelong bay-side property owners can protect their concrete from salt, moisture, and weather.
body: Owning a property near Geelong's beautiful coastline comes with unique advantages and challenges, especially when it comes to concrete work. From the popular beachside suburbs of Belmont and East Geelong to the rapidly growing areas around Lara and Point Henry, proximity to Corio Bay and Bass Strait means your concrete structures face constant exposure to salt air, wind-driven moisture, and fluctuating humidity levels. At Vik Concreting Geelong, with over seven years of experience serving the region's coastal properties, we understand the specific demands that Geelong's bay-side environment places on concrete surfaces. Whether you are building a new driveway, installing a pool surround, or constructing a commercial slab near the waterfront, choosing the right materials and methods is essential for longevity. This guide explores the key considerations for concrete work on Geelong's coastal properties.

The primary challenge for concrete near Geelong's coast is salt-induced degradation, commonly known as concrete cancer or spalling. Salt-laden air from Corio Bay and the Southern Ocean penetrates concrete over time, reaching the steel reinforcement within and causing it to corrode and expand. This expansion creates internal pressure that eventually cracks and flakes the concrete surface, a process that can begin within five to ten years if the concrete is not properly protected. Geelong suburbs closest to the bay, including East Geelong, Breakwater, Moolap, and Point Henry, experience the highest levels of salt exposure and require particularly robust concrete specifications. Using high-quality, low-permeability concrete mixes with adequate cover over reinforcement steel is the first line of defence. Vik Concreting Geelong specifies marine-grade reinforcement and dense concrete mixes for all coastal projects to ensure maximum protection against Geelong's salt-rich environment.

Surface treatments and sealers play a critical role in protecting coastal concrete in Geelong from moisture and salt ingress. A high-quality penetrating sealer creates an invisible barrier within the concrete pores that repels water and dissolved salts without altering the surface appearance. For exposed aggregate driveways and decorative concrete surfaces near the coast, an acrylic or polyurethane sealer adds an additional protective layer that shields the finish from UV degradation and salt damage. In Geelong's coastal suburbs, resealing should be carried out every two to three years to maintain optimal protection, as the combination of salt spray and strong UV exposure during summer can break down sealers faster than in inland areas. Vik Concreting Geelong uses only premium-grade sealers suited to the local conditions and offers ongoing maintenance programs for coastal property owners who want to keep their concrete in peak condition for decades.

Geelong's coastal properties also face drainage challenges that directly affect concrete performance. Many older beachside suburbs have established drainage systems that may not cope with increased impervious surfaces like new driveways or large concrete slabs. When you replace a permeable surface with concrete, you must ensure that stormwater runoff is properly managed to avoid pooling, erosion, or non-compliance with City of Greater Geelong Council regulations. In low-lying coastal areas such as Moolap and parts of East Geelong, high water tables can cause hydrostatic pressure beneath concrete slabs, leading to rising damp and surface deterioration. Proper site assessment before any concrete pour is essential, and Vik Concreting Geelong always conducts thorough ground evaluations for coastal projects to identify potential drainage issues and design appropriate solutions before work begins.

For Geelong homeowners with coastal properties considering new concrete work, material selection is paramount. Standard concrete mixes that perform well in inland suburbs may degrade prematurely near the bay. Vik Concreting Geelong recommends using sulphate-resistant cement, which provides enhanced protection against the chemical attack caused by salt and mineral-rich groundwater common in coastal Geelong. Additionally, incorporating synthetic fibres or welded wire mesh reinforcement improves the concrete's resistance to cracking caused by thermal movement and shrinkage, both of which are amplified in coastal environments where temperature swings between day and night can be significant. For pool surrounds, which are particularly popular in Geelong's beachside suburbs, a slip-resistant exposed aggregate or textured finish provides both safety and style while standing up to constant exposure to chlorinated or saltwater splashes.

Whether you are planning a new driveway in East Geelong, a commercial slab near the Geelong waterfront, or a pool surround in Belmont, choosing a concreter with genuine local coastal experience is essential. Generic concrete advice from inland-focused contractors often overlooks the specific challenges that Geelong's bay-side environment presents. Vik Concreting Geelong has spent seven years pouring concrete across the region's most demanding coastal sites, and we know exactly which mixes, reinforcements, and finishes deliver lasting results. Our team stays up to date with the latest Australian standards for coastal construction, including AS 3600 for concrete structures and relevant City of Greater Geelong Council requirements. For a free assessment of your coastal concrete project in Geelong, contact Vik Concreting Geelong on 0403 964 510 or request a quote online. We proudly serve Geelong, Lara, Belmont, East Geelong, and all surrounding coastal suburbs.
